ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der. Proto-Italic *-iðos Latin -idus Latin vīviduslbor. English vivid Learned borrowing from Latin vividus (“animated, spirited”), from vivere (“to live”), akin to vita (“life”), Ancient Greek βίος (bíos, “life”). The noun sense (a type of marker pen) was genericized from Bic's Vivid Marker brand.

senses.d: A felt-tipped permanent marker; a marker pen.

ety.text: Inherited from Latin clārus. Compare Albanian qartë.
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der. Proto-Italic *-iðos Latin -idus Latin vīvidusbor. Spanish vívido Borrowed from Latin vīvidus.
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der. Proto-Italic *-iðos Latin -idus Latin vividusbor. Portuguese vívido Borrowed from Latin vividus.

Latin vīvusinflu. Spanish vivo Inherited from Old Spanish bivo, vivo, from Latin vīvus. The dissimilated bivo was most common during the Middle Ages (compare Old Spanish bivir and bolver), with vivo becoming the standard form during the Spanish Golden Age for its semblance to the Latin etymon.
From Old Galician-Portuguese vivo, from Latin vīvus, from Proto-Italic *gʷīwos, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃wós.
